ai_show_review.summary: Strong early‑70 set with stellar High Time and tight jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The show shines on High Time, Cryptical Envelopment into Black Peter, and Black Peter itself. Jerry’s vocals are spot‑on and his backup work in Dancin’ In The Street is praised, while the rhythm section drives powerfully. The mix is crisp and balanced despite a few cuts that interrupt parts of the set.
ai_show_review.review: On February 6, 1970 at San Francisco’s Fillmore West, the Dead delivered an early‑70s set that balances laid‑back country numbers with lingering psychedelic jams. Highlights include a soaring High Time, the seamless segue from Cryptical Envelopment into Black Peter, and a heartfelt rendition of Black Peter itself. Jerry Garcia sings “his heart out,” his lead vocal staying spot‑on while backing harmonies lift Dancin’ In The Street. Bob Weir cuts through the mix with crisp guitar work, Phil Lesh provides a solid bass foundation (even bobbing his head in time), and the twin drummers, Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann, lay down a powerful, driving beat that propels the band forward. The soundboard capture is unusually clear for the era—crisp, balanced, and with vocals and instruments well defined—though six noticeable cuts (including portions of Dancin’ In The Street) and occasional speed irregularities detract from an otherwise solid listening experience.

best_recording.reason: Good soundboard source with crisp, balanced mix; despite a few cuts it offers the clearest representation of the performance.
